question: Admit the 65 test changes `verify:test-replay` refuses (verdicts `test-expectation-changed` / `test-removed`)? That gate replays each test's old body against the new code, so a branch can't quietly loosen a test. Five read-only reviewers compared all 59 P2 rewrites old against new, looking for weakening. Results: 21 STRENGTHENED (a silent `return`, which used to pass whenever a tool or env was missing, now fails or is a `cfg!` arm; a test that read the real checkout or used a stale binary now builds its own fixture; a timing ceiling became an exact recorded outcome, e.g. the second-signal case now proves an escalation actually happened, which the old 4s ceiling never did). 32 EQUIVALENT (same assertions, different mechanism; mostly the old body no longer compiles because a skip helper was replaced). 2 SUBJECT-CHANGED (`symbols` analyses a toy crate instead of the whole crate, to drop a 38-54s clippy run and a target-dir deadlock). 4 WEAKENED, each now addressed: (1) the `symbols` toy lost coverage of the engine's launcher, so I added `the_engine_launcher_mediates_a_pinned_tree_and_runs_bare_elsewhere`; (2) the `pr_watch` e2e no longer proved the `X-Poll-Interval` header reaches the loop, so the parse is now one `poll_floor_of`, pinned by a unit test and a mutant; (3) the hanging session step would pass if the drain hung 30s, so it now sleeps 3600s and a failure to kill runs into nextest's time limit and fails; (4) `the_hook_path_never_updates`: "a hook never downloads" is dropped, deliberately, per your pin-following instruction; the fetch-failure fallback is covered by main's `adjudicate_absent` cases.
